Topic 29 -- Intro to Differential Equations 
Some Definitions 
A differential equation is an equation that contains an unknown 
function and some of its derivatives. 
The order of a differential equation is the order of the highest 
derivative that occurs in the equation. 
For this introduction, we will only consider “ordinary” differential 
equations (i.e. equations that contain ordinary derivatives).

Definition of solution 
A function 𝑓 is called a solution of a differential equation if the 
equation is satisfied when 𝑦 = 𝑓(𝑥) and its derivatives are substituted 
into the equation.

Introduction to Modeling 
When a physical situation includes a rate of change, it may be 
modeled with a differential equation. 
Example 9 
“Suppose a population grows at a rate proportional to its size.”

Example 10 
“Suppose the rate at which a rumor is spreading in a fixed population 
is proportional to the product of the number of people that have heard 
the rumor and the number of people that have not heard the rumor.”
